explanation: Taste sensors on their legs let a female test a leaf before she lays eggs on it. She drums on it with her feet to release its juices, checking it will suit her caterpillars.

claims.text: Butterflies have taste receptors on their feet.
Female butterflies use taste receptors on their legs to test plants before laying eggs on them.
Some female butterflies drum on leaves with their feet to release plant juices for tasting.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: three listed; high: c1 (checker_doubt, standing in for counterintuitive, which the tooling's riskReason enum lacks; C26 makes the key of a counterintuitive item high); standard: c2 and c3. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology (it holds countries, languages, currencies, cities, elements, Nobel Prizes, Olympic Games, World Cups, art collections and Natural Earth), so none applies, and the high-risk claims need web evidence from checker A; one search on butterflies tasting with their feet should cover c1 to c3. rivalTest: Argued for false: the statement sounds like a children's-book exaggeration, and butterflies also taste with their mouthparts. But chemoreceptors on the tarsi are well documented, and 'can taste with' claims only that the feet taste, not that they are the only organ. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: butterflies live on every continent apart from Antarctica. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 34 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a true/false item. doubts: none on the key; c3 is hedged with 'some' because drumming is documented in swallowtails and monarchs rather than in every butterfly.

evidence.restatement: Butterflies carry taste (contact chemoreceptor) sensilla on the tarsi of their legs, so they taste what they stand on.

evidence.restatement: Egg-laying females use these leg receptors to recognize a suitable host plant before laying.
Females of many species drum or scratch the leaf with their forelegs, breaking the surface so the leg receptors can sample the plant's juices.
Butterflies carry taste (contact chemoreceptor) organs on their feet.
Egg-laying females test a plant by tasting it with their foot receptors before they lay.
Females of some species drum a leaf with their forelegs, which breaks surface cells and releases juices they can taste.
